probe: whether a project settings file can isolate the logger's home for self-application
method: A scratch project whose .claude/settings.local.json sets env.KO_QUALITY_HOME to a scratch directory. Run 1: the same file also registers SessionStart and Stop command hooks that append the variable's value to a file. Run 2: the hooks are removed, and the shipped logger is loaded through --plugin-dir dist/claude-code/agent-reply. KO_QUALITY_HOME was not set in the launching shell for either run. Two headless runs; cost not captured.

results.q: Does `env` in a project's .claude/settings.local.json reach command hooks?
results.a: Yes. Both SessionStart and Stop saw KO_QUALITY_HOME set to the settings value.

results.q: Does it reach a plugin's hooks, that is, the shipped logger?
results.a: Yes. The logger wrote one record to <scratch>/home-from-settings/logs/agent-reply/2026-09.jsonl. ~/.ko-quality was absent before and after the run.

findings: Isolation can be configured per project in one settings line, with no change to the plugin or the shell.

.claude/settings.local.json is gitignored in this repository. Isolation written there is per machine and not versioned: a fresh clone, or a session on another machine, writes into the default home with nothing in the record to show where it came from.

The logger reads KO_QUALITY_HOME with Path(...) and does not expand `~`. A committed .claude/settings.json cannot carry a portable value without either a machine-specific absolute path (forbidden by AGENTS.md) or a one-line expanduser in the logger. Whether Claude Code itself expands `~` in settings env was not tested.
The record has no field that identifies the originating project. The Stop payload carries `cwd` (tests/runs/02-E6/stop-hook-gate.json), but the logger does not keep it.
cleanup: Scratch directory only. No user or repository settings were modified.
